slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 5:24: Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.
slides.body: “Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.”
slides.heading: Gen 5:24

slides.alt_text: Slide one introduces the claim that Enoch's disappearance foreshadows Jesus' ascension.
slides.body: Genesis says God took Enoch. The New Testament says Jesus was taken into heaven. Some Christians see Enoch's mysterious departure as an early illustration of Christ's ascension.
slides.heading: Did Enoch foreshadow the ascension?

slides.alt_text: Slide two presents the Christian typological case based on Enoch's exception to death and Hebrews 11:5.
slides.body: Enoch alone escapes Genesis 5's repeated ‘and he died.’ Hebrews says he was taken so that he did not see death. Typology need not be a verbal prediction: this exceptional departure can serve as an early pattern of bodily translation into God's presence.
slides.heading: The strongest Christian case

slides.alt_text: Slide three concludes that Enoch provides plausible typology but not a direct prediction of Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis never describes heaven or a body rising. Enoch avoids death; Jesus dies, rises, then ascends. No New Testament text calls Jesus' ascension a fulfilment of Enoch's story. The link works as later Christian typology—not as a prediction in Genesis.
slides.heading: A real parallel—with limits

title: Does Enoch's disappearance foreshadow Jesus' ascension?
